answer_1.quote: In this paper, we present BBAEG (Biomedical BERT-based Adversarial Example Generation) 1 , a novel black-box attack algorithm for biomedical text classification task leveraging both the BERT-MLM model for non-named entity replacements combined with NER linked synonyms for named entities to better fit the overall context.
answer_1.outputs: adversarial examples for biomedical text classification

answer_2.quote: We examine the success of adversarial attack using two criteria: (1) Performance Drop (Adrop): Difference between original (accuracy on original test set) and afterattack accuracy (accuracy on the perturbed test set) (2) Perturbation of input (%): Percentage of perturbed words in adversary generated.

answer_4.quote: Through human evaluation, we show that BBAEG yields adversarial examples with improved naturalness.
answer_4.guideline: During ablation analysis, we observe that the synonym replaced perturbed samples looked more natural to the human evaluators compared to the spelling perturbed samples and number replaced entities. When considered jointly, the number replaced and synonym replaced samples seemed more natural to the annotators compared to spelling perturbed samples.
